answer: Behavioral Lagoon Clustering. Each agent's action trace is embedded and clustered; new identities whose traces sit inside an existing cluster's lagoon of correlated behavior get merged, and merged identities share one reputation weight. Honest agents drift apart over time, so separation is cheap for them. An attacker must run each fake identity through distinct, sustained behavioral histories long enough to clear the ridge separating clusters, paying full operating cost per identity for months before it counts.
